prompt: In the pipeline `grep ' 404 ' access.log | cut -d' ' -f1 | sort | uniq -c`, what is actually on `uniq -c`'s stdin?
choices: The raw, unfiltered lines of access.log
The sorted output of the `sort` stage
The unsorted IP addresses straight from `cut`
A line count produced by `wc -l`

prompt: Why does `uniq -c` typically need its input piped through `sort` first?
choices: sort reduces the file size so uniq runs faster
uniq only collapses consecutive duplicate lines, so duplicates must already be adjacent
uniq requires numerically sorted input or it errors out
uniq cannot read from a pipe at all, only from a sorted file on disk

prompt: You need to know which `sort` flag makes it compare a column as a number (so 9 sorts before 10) instead of as text. What's the right move?
choices: Try random single-letter flags until one happens to work
Check `man sort` or `sort --help` for a numeric-comparison option
Pre-sort the data manually before piping it into sort
Skip sort entirely and write a script instead

choices: Git Bash just runs git commands slightly slower
WSL2 runs an actual Linux kernel with a real package manager and a working Docker daemon; Git Bash is a POSIX-style shell layer on top of the Windows NT kernel with no Linux kernel underneath
